title: help --why still disagrees with the refusal when devbin's handler is missing, and 0111's arms hold less than they appear to
body:
FOUND by cc's independent review of 0111 on 2026-09-23 (hv: "Yes"). 0111 is closed and shipped in 0.1.7, and this changes no release already cut. The review ran against 142763d, 0.1.7's release commit. It re-ran the new arms against the pre-fix code, drove each case in scratch fixtures, and ran 17 mutants against the five bats files 0111 and 0112 touched (239 arms; the baseline was green, 239/239).

WHAT HOLDS. Every new or changed arm fails against the pre-fix code, and each fails for the reason it names (9 of 9). Twelve of the seventeen mutants are killed. Among them is the first cut vc's commit describes, killed by exactly one arm, the older `db all` one, as the commit says.

1. THE TWO SURFACES STILL DISAGREE WHEN DEVBIN'S HANDLER IS MISSING. 0111 says the refusal and `help --why` "cannot drift again", and the 0.1.7 note repeats it. That holds for a name-only built-in, where command_origin calls unrunnable_why, and it does not hold for a partial install. Both of these were driven in fixtures:
   - With `lib/cmd/version` removed, `bin/devbin version` says "devbin's handler for 'version' is missing from this install", while `help --why` says `from: devbin catalogue`.
   - With `lib/cmd/check` removed, `check format` gives the same refusal, while `--why` says `check` comes `from: its options` and every option `from: devbin catalogue`.
   The catalogue runs none of them: the rows say `@builtin`, which means the handler was meant to. The cause is that command_origin and option_origin reach for the catalogue through builtin_has_default_run and builtin_option_run, and both count `@builtin` as a command line. The refusal is right and `--why` is wrong, which is the same shape 0111 was filed for, one case over.

2. TWO BRANCHES OF unrunnable_why ARE REACHED BY NO CALLER:
   - The lookup-failure branch (`run=""` when builtin_option_run fails).
   - The name-only OPTION sentence ("declare commands.X.options.Y.run").
   None of the three callers can reach either. run_option calls report_unrunnable only inside `if builtin_option_run ... ; then`. Every built-in has a command row. command_origin calls unrunnable_why only for a built-in. A project-declared command with no run, handler or options is inactive (exit 2) and never reaches run_command, which was driven. Mutants on both branches survive all 239 arms. If a future caller did reach the lookup failure, it would say "devbin ships the name only" of a name devbin does not ship.

3. THREE THINGS THE ARMS DO NOT HOLD, each shown by a surviving mutant:
   - (a) THE REFUSAL'S STREAM. report_unrunnable writes to stderr, and nothing holds it there. The mutant that sends both lines to stdout survives, because bats `run` merges the streams. The helper 0111 moved these sites off, not_yet, has had a stream arm since the start (helpers.bats, "not_yet names the gate and exits 3"), and it was not carried over.
   - (b) THE REMEDY IS CHECKED BY SUBSTRING. The contract and surfaces arms assert `commands.build.run`, and `commands.build.runs` contains it. So a remedy naming a key the validator would refuse passes every arm, the ONE-answer arm included, since both surfaces change together. The strong form is to declare the key the refusal names and see the command run.
   - (c) THE CHECKOUT'S SEAM LINE. 8a8d1ae added a second wording of the overview's seam line for devbin's own checkout ("devbin's source -- this tree; nothing vendored"). Making the checkout print the install's wording instead survives: the checkout arm checks only that the paths exist.

4. PROSE LEFT DESCRIBING THE OLD REFUSAL:
   - run_command's header in lib/resolve still ends its order with "otherwise nothing runs it, which is the not-yet case".
   - intent/llm/ARCHITECTURE-shell.md's resolution order ends "otherwise not-yet, exit 3".
   - intent/llm/MODULES.md's resolution row ends "-> not-yet, exit 3".
   - Separately, and older: a comment in command_active in lib/resolve says WP-18's enablement axis is "not yet built", five lines above the block that builds it.

CHECKED AND SOUND, so nobody chases it. 774104b's arm pipes into `grep -q` under release.bats's top-level `set -euo pipefail`, the shape of 0031. By 0031's own refined rule it is sound: the only line that can match is the last line `grep -A1` emits, so the reader cannot decide before the writer is done.

## Resolution

Fixed at 70faf4c. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. help --why, doctor and the refusal give one answer when devbin's handler is missing. builtin_has_default_run stops counting @builtin, which fixes help --why and doctor's runnable check in one place, and option_origin asks for the handler as run_option does. unrunnable_why's two unreachable branches are gone. A name the catalogue lacks now prints a devbin defect line and returns (cc's review), with an arm that calls it directly, since no caller reaches it. Arms hold the refusal's stream, its remedy key and the checkout's seam line, and four stale not-yet descriptions are fixed.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. Three arms are red at the base. K1-K5 are killed. K6, the fmt arms asking builtin_has_default_run, is an equivalence probe: check format's full output was measured identical either way. On cc's note, N1-N3 are killed.
- REVIEW. cc: sound.
- LEFT OPEN. 0128's D2-tiers refactor reaches command_origin and _command_runnable, and these arms hold them through it.
- THE SUITE. The full suite on the series as it landed -- land018 at c130b3a, whose 27 series paths are byte-identical to the landed commits: 1..1653, 1653 ok, 0 not ok, 4 skips (127, 135, 624, 626), rc 0, 12:39:28Z to 13:11:35Z. Each commit passed the gate (guards, critic, doctor) as it landed.
